fixes.explanation: Not in this verse, friend. The LORD says what His children did, and it's “…they have rebelled against Me.” Nothing here mentions a king. Stay in verse 2 and the answer is sitting right there.

It's the other way around, friend. The ox knows its owner and the donkey its master's manger, “…but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.” The animals are the ones in the picture who know. I think that's a hard line to hear, and the LORD says it plainly.

Right, it's False. The ox knows its owner and the donkey its master's manger, “…but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.” The animals are the ones in the picture who know. It's a simple comparison, and it stings.
Not quite, baker. Isaiah says they “…have despised the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on Him.” Fearing Him isn't the word he uses. Despised and turned their backs is what the verse says.

It's True, friend. Isaiah says the sores were “…neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.” Nobody cleaned them, wrapped them or soothed them. Read the verse again and all three are right there.

Nobles are a fair guess, but the verse points somewhere else. Isaiah says, “Foreigners devour your fields before you…” The ones doing the devouring are outsiders, and the verse calls them strangers. Those are the words to hold onto.

Close the guest list, friend. Isaiah says the Daughter of Zion “…is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field…” The picture is abandoned, not crowded. A shack left alone in a field has plenty of room.

That's not the picture, friend. Isaiah says the Daughter of Zion “…is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field…” The word he uses is abandoned. Think of a shack left alone in a field.

Prophets aren't in this verse. Isaiah says, “Unless the LORD of Hosts had left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.” The word is survivors. A few of them is the whole difference.

That title isn't in this verse, baker. Isaiah says, “Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!” Calling them rulers of Sodom is a sharp thing to say to people in charge. It's the name he picks for them, and it's not a friendly one.

It's True, friend. The LORD says, “…I cannot endure iniquity in a solemn assembly.” That comes right after He names New Moons, Sabbaths and convocations. So what He can't endure is iniquity showing up in the middle of those gatherings.
Yes, their evil deeds. The LORD says, “Remove your evil deeds from My sight. Stop doing evil!” Right alongside “Wash and cleanse yourselves,” He tells them to stop. The deeds are what He wants gone.

The king and his court aren't named in this verse. The LORD says, “Defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.” He points to the fatherless and the widow, not to people in high places. I think that tells us who He wants them looking out for.

Priests and Levites don't show up in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “Defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.” Those are the two He names, and they're the ones to stand up for. Defend and plead are things you do, not just things you feel.
